summary: Air Warning Service station cabin on Ozette Lake, activated in November 1942 and abandoned when the service ended; the cabin is gone.

facts.status_note: The cabin is gone; no source describes what remains at the point.

events.note: AWS station activated 23 November 1942 under the Port Angeles Filter Center; cabin constructed
Date given by firelookout.com. Forest Lookouts quotes a May 1, 1944 AWS report on the abandonment; the sources disagree on the year.

evidence.supports: location on east side of Ozette Lake
AWS station activated 23 Nov 1942, Port Angeles Filter Center
evidence.quote: Activated: November 23, 1942. Port Angeles Filter Center.

evidence.supports: AWS expands to Air Warning Service

evidence.quote: The AWS constructed a 14 x 32 cabin

evidence.supports: abandoned at end of service because state did not want it
evidence.quote: At the end of service the site was abandoned as the State did not want.

evidence.supports: account attributed to May 1, 1944 AWS report
May 1, 1944 date of the AWS stations report

evidence.quote: AWS Ozette Lake Clallam 48.08230 -124.61976 Ground Gone

notes_for_editor: Abandonment year conflicts: 1945 (firelookout.com) against the end-of-service account citing a May 1, 1944 AWS report (Forest Lookouts). Only two detailed sources exist, and neither describes the site today. The Forest Lookouts text spells the lake 'Lake Osette', an apparent typo for Ozette. The FFLA list also has a separate 'AWS Ozette Beach' entry at 48.05932, -124.69285 (Gone), which may be a different site; not checked. firelookout.com lists 'Washington Division of Forestry/DNR' near the top of its page, but the role of that line (agency or owner) is unclear, so no agency is recorded. The record's agency is null.
